newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat stabilises as quality fears ease.
newsitem.headline: French wheat stabilises as quality fears ease.

text.p: French wheat prices stabilised on Thursday as reports from the fields eased fears that June rains had seriously cut milling wheat quality, dealers said.

Sellers, who feared they could not guaranteee good wheat quality, had bought back their positions in recent days, underpinning prices in the Moselle, Rhin and Chalons/Modane areas. But reports that the situation was not as bad as anticipated stopped the buying spree.
"Reports are a little less negative and this is making buyers a little less nervous," one dealer said.

Officials from the local ONIC grain offices in northern and eastern France have however said that June rain could reduce wheat yields and quality though it was too early to assess the extent of the damage.
Fob Moselle wheat for August rose to 900 francs per tonne this week. It was offered at that level on Thursday but there were no buyers.
Rouen wheat for August was steady at 850-855 francs depending on silos as there was no fresh export news to move prices.
The European Union's grain management committee that adjudicates grain exports is not meeting this week due to two-week gaps between tenders in July and August.
The focus is also turning to Egypt's tender for 50,000 tonnes of French soft wheat due next weekend.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
